- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 15–30% for next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.67), model underestimates; increase forecast by 15–30% for next 3–5 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 3x recent mean), model often overcorrects; apply a “lag correction” — reduce forecast by 20–40% for 2–4 days post-spike.  
- If forecast is consistently > true outcome by 20%+ over 3–5 days, apply “mean reversion” rule: subtract 10–20% of forecast from next 3–5 days’ values.  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and forecast is high, model often fails to capture downward trend; reduce forecast by 10–25% for next 3–5 days.  
- For 30-day horizon, if forecast is > 2x true outcome, apply “horizon decay” — scale down by 10–15% per day for next 5 days.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67, -0.67, 0.67), model tends to overreact; apply “sentiment dampening” — reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 3–5 days.
